historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-period base-case consolidated growth (product sales +4-5%/yr net of VBP erosion as innovative launches scale, plus a normalised licence stream). Equity 5yr CAGR of 8.2% is not used because it is inflated by retained licence cash and understated distributions, and the trailing revenue/EPS/FCF CAGRs are all negative through the FY2024-25 VBP trough.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR +3.2% vs revenue -5.6% and EPS -12.7%: equity kept compounding through buybacks and retained cash while the P&L shrank under VBP/NRDL price cuts. FY2025 owner FCF of 3,356m is a trough (oncology -50%, tax paid 824m); H1 FY2026 owner FCF of ~9,660m is a licence windfall. Neither is a base.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (floored at 0 in FY2025) - interest income: FY2020 5,250.0; FY2022 4,519.1; FY2025 3,356.2. Owner-FCF CAGRs (-9.4%/-8.6%) are slightly better than reported (-10.3%/-7.9%) because interest income fell with Chinese deposit rates; SBC is immaterial throughout.

scenario_narratives.base: Licence fee income normalises from the H1 FY2026 windfall (5.9bn) to a recurring ~3-4bn stream, product sales grind +4-5% as the innovative launch cycle (Enshuxing, Enyitan, nanocrystal/liposome lines, EU Ansulike) outruns the next VBP rounds, and segment EBITDA margin recovers from the FY2025 trough (22.8%) to the FY2022-23 level (28%) on lower selling expense and mix. Capex elevated for the AstraZeneca biologics JV plant then tapers. The FY2027 revenue decline is the licence reset, not a product decline.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AstraZeneca partnership converts into a durable annuity: milestones on US$28bn of contract value begin to pay, further deals (ADC, siRNA, CAR-T, GLP-1/GIP) add partners, licence fees run 5-7bn/yr at ~100% margin, product sales grow 8% as oncology/autoimmune launches scale and the 15th Five-Year Plan favours innovation incumbents. Blended EBITDA 32%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Single-counterparty and single-regulator risks both bite: BD appetite cools and AstraZeneca slows, licence fees fall to ~1.5bn; successive VBP/NRDL rounds take another 3%/yr off product sales for three years (a repeat of FY2025's oncology -50%), bulk APIs stay oversupplied, R&D intensity cannot be cut without hollowing the pipeline, and the HNTE tax concession lapses. Margins stuck at the FY2025 trough and the exit multiple compresses to 12x.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the cash the product business and the R&D-funded licensing engine throw off together, strip the one-off H1 FY2026 licence windfall into the balance sheet where it already sits (net cash RMB22.1bn before the 1,480m dividend payable and 2,460m refundable upfront), and charge VBP, counterparty and pipeline risk once, in the scenario weights rather than the discount rate. The business is worth its product franchise (NBP, Mingfule, the sales force) plus a probability-weighted BD stream, not the H1 FY2026 print.
key_risks_to_valuation: Licence fee normalisation level: every RMB1bn/yr of recurring licence income is worth roughly RMB0.9-1.0/share (HK$1.1) at 8%/15x; the base assumes 3-4bn, H1 FY2026 alone was 5.9bn and FY2025 was 1.8bn
VBP/NRDL rounds cutting product sales faster than the 4-5% base-case growth (FY2025 oncology -50%, Duomeisu -97% in the national round)
AstraZeneca counterparty concentration: the 2,460m refundable upfront and most of the US$28bn contract value depend on one partner's continued priorities
Terminal multiple: the 15x cap binds in base and bull (Gordon at 8%/2.5% implies 18.6x); the valuation is ~55% terminal value
HNTE 15% tax concession expiring 2027 and the 750m/yr of unrecognised losses in loss-making R&D subsidiaries
RMB/HKD: all per-share values are translated at 1.1722; a 5% RMB move is ~HK$0.50/share

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E = H1 FY2026 actual RMB18,594m + H2 estimate RMB13,500m (sales of goods ~12,500m, +4% on H2 FY2025's 12,018m, plus ~1,000m H2 licence fees incl. the July-2026 AstraZeneca kidney deal upfront). FY2026E splits ~25,200m sales of goods / ~6,900m licence fee income. The year-1 (FY2027) growth rate of -9% is the licence-fee normalisation from ~6.9bn to a 3.0bn run-rate, NOT a product-sales decline.
inputs.cash_note: 30 June 2026: bank deposits, balances and cash 14,177.1m (incl. 4,386.1m time deposits >3m and 4,175.6m non-current deposits) less 124.7m pledged/restricted = 14,052.4m, plus structured bank deposits (FVTPL, guaranteed-return bank products) 8,485.9m = 22,538.3m. Interest on all of it is the stripped stream. The 1,480m FY2025 final dividend payable and the 2,460m refundable AstraZeneca upfront (other payables note 18) are deducted in equity_bridge, not here, so each is visible.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR cash-flow statement: share-based payment expense was a REVERSAL of RMB-65.9m (lapse of the Sept-2023 management option grant); floored at zero for the owner-FCF anchor. Forward charge set at 0.6% of revenue (~RMB175m/yr) because the trustee share-award scheme is now funded in cash (RMB279.7m of shares purchased in H1 FY2026, 'Purchase of shares under share award scheme', interim CF statement) and the awards will expense as they vest.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow: RMB277.6m repurchase and cancellation (64.3m shares). H1 FY2026: nil cancellation buyback but RMB279.7m of trustee purchases for the share award scheme. The flat count is funded.
inputs.share_count_basis: 11,419.9m = weighted-average DILUTED shares for H1 FY2026 (interim note 6: basic 11,401.2m net of trustee-held award shares + 18.7m options/awards). Held FLAT: SBC charged in the flows at 0.6% of revenue, so diluting the count as well would double-charge. Buybacks in FY2024-25 cancelled ~350m shares; no non-SBC issuance is expected.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. fx_rate 1.1722 HKD per CNY from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-11T14:37Z. Per-share values are computed in RMB and multiplied by 1.1722 to HKD. No dual listing exists for a parity check (CSPC has no A-share); cross-check: the HK$0.18 interim dividend equals RMB0.154/share at this rate, consistent with the RMB-denominated dividend payable of 1,480m for the HK$0.15 final on ~11.4bn shares (HK$1.71bn / 1.1722 = RMB1.46bn, within 1.5%).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z regular close (HKEX; Friday close, not after-hours)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in the flows' currency (RMB): China 10y CGB ~1.8% (Oct-2026) + China equity risk premium ~6.2% x beta ~1.0 for a large-cap HK-listed China pharma = ~8.0% cost of equity; borrowings are 1% of equity so WACC = CoE = 8.0%. The same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios: VBP/NRDL pricing risk, AstraZeneca counterparty concentration and pipeline attrition are charged ONCE, in the scenario flows and weights, not via a per-scenario or ad-hoc WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: full lease cash (FY2025 principal 138.9m + interest 9.9m = 148.8m, 0.57% of revenue; H1 FY2026 70.8m) charged inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path 0.5%; lease liabilities (249.2m at 30 June 2026) EXCLUDED from total_debt, which is bank borrowings only (128.9m current + 274.4m non-current = 403.3m, ties to the MD&A gearing of 1.0%). D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 1,412.8m total less ~180m RoU = ~1,233m = 4.7% of revenue; H1 FY2026 RoU depreciation 78.4m) so the lease is not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI book value RMB1,807.2m at 30 June 2026 deducted ONCE in the equity bridge. NCI profit share was -5.7m in FY2025 and 10.8m in FY2024 but 366.0m in H1 FY2026 (a licence deal struck in a partly-owned subsidiary), so the bridge deduction at book is the conservative single charge.
inputs.non_operating_assets: Other financial assets (FVTPL/FVOCI investments, 2,138.6m non-current + 59.1m current = 2,197.7m) and interests in associates/JVs (575.0m + 603.3m = 1,178.3m) are added in the bridge at book because their income (fair-value gains, dividends, share of results) is EXCLUDED from the EBITDA build, which is segment profit + D&A. Matching-asset rule: every stripped stream has its asset in the bridge.
inputs.licence_fee_treatment: Licence fee income (RMB1,789m FY2025, RMB5,895m H1 FY2026 incl. the US$1.2bn Jan-2026 AstraZeneca obesity upfront) is real, high-margin revenue earned by the ~RMB6bn/yr R&D programme, so it is NOT stripped; but H1 FY2026 is NOT a run-rate. Base case normalises it to RMB3.0bn in FY2027 rising to ~4bn by FY2030 (management: 'stable, recurring revenue stream'; five deals since 2025 with US$28bn contract value, mostly back-ended milestones). Bull ~5-7bn (milestones flow, new deals); bear ~1.5bn (China-to-West BD boom cools, AstraZeneca re-prioritises). The windfall cash already received is captured in the 30 June 2026 net cash. The refundable 2,460m upfront is deducted as debt-like; the 1,491.7m non-refundable contract liabilities are left as ordinary deferred revenue because the forward licence stream is a normalised, not cash-matched, figure.
inputs.stub_period_note: Net cash is at 30 June 2026; year-1 flow is FY2027. H2 FY2026 owner FCF (~RMB1.5-2bn) is in neither, and the HK18c interim dividend (~RMB1.75bn, record date 26 Oct 2026, payable 10 Nov 2026) is paid out of it to the holder at today's price. The two roughly offset and both are left out.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating pharma company; routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2, non-US operating company, with the adaptations: RMB-built WACC, CNY->HKD bridge, lease treatment B, NCI once, matching-asset rule). First valuation of this ticker. EBITDA basis = reportable-segment profit + D&A (FY2025: 4,522.9m + 1,412.8m = 5,935.7m = 22.8% of revenue incl. licence fees; ex-licence ~17.1%; H1 FY2026 ex-licence ~18.2%), which excludes other income (government grants 210m, interest 196m), FVTPL gains, and associates. FY2025 underlying profit fell 24.5% vs reported -10.3%: the reported figure was flattered by 258m of FVTPL gains and the SBC reversal, so the margin anchor is the segment measure, not reported profit. Cash tax: FY2025 effective 19.4%, cash paid 824m (17% of PBT) with 750m/yr of unrecognised tax losses in R&D subs and HNTE 15% relief running to 2027 -> base ramps 18% to 20%. Working capital: receivables + bills 7.4bn + inventories 3.0bn vs payables + bills 2.7bn (~30% of revenue) -> wc_capture -20% (growth consumes cash; the FY2027 licence normalisation releases it). Terminal cap 15x owner FCF (Gordon at 8%/2.5% = 18.6x would bind otherwise): today's EV/FY2027E owner FCF is ~15x, so no multiple expansion is assumed. SBC-zero-ish market: SBC held visible at 0.6%; house/street band is narrow but non-zero.

bear.narrative: The China-to-West BD boom cools and AstraZeneca re-prioritises: licence fees fall to ~1.5bn and stay there; VBP batch 11+ and NRDL renegotiations cut product sales 3%/yr for three years (oncology/anti-infective repeat of FY2025) before flat-lining; bulk vitamin C/antibiotic overcapacity persists. Ex-licence EBITDA stuck at the FY2025 trough (~17%), blended 21%. HNTE 15% relief lapses after 2027 (tax 22%). Terminal cap cut to 12x for a shrinking regulated-price book.

base.narrative: FY2027 revenue ~29.2bn = sales of goods 26.2bn (+4%) + licence 3.0bn; licence rises to ~4bn by FY2030 while product sales grow 5% as Enshuxing, Enyitan, Mingfule (AHA/ASA 2026 guideline) and NBP (2026 NEML) offset continuing VBP rounds. Blended EBITDA (segment basis) 26% rising to 28%, the FY2022-23 level, as selling expense keeps falling and mix shifts to innovative drugs. Capex 7.5% (biologics JV plant) easing to 5.5%.

bull.narrative: Licence fees settle at ~5bn in FY2027 and compound to ~7bn as AstraZeneca milestones (US$28bn contract value across obesity/T2DM, kidney, ADC, Lp(a)) start paying and new partners are added; product sales grow 8% on the innovative launch cycle and the 15th Five-Year Plan pillar-industry tailwind. Blended EBITDA reaches 32% (licence ~15% of revenue at ~100% margin). Same 8% WACC; terminal growth 3%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30% because two concentration risks are live at once: a single regulator (VBP/NRDL, with batch 11 and the April-2026 pricing-mechanism opinions already scheduled) controls pricing on ~75% of revenue, and a single counterparty (AstraZeneca) supplies most of the licence stream that the base case treats as recurring. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right: milestones paying, new partners signing, AND product-sales acceleration through further VBP rounds. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
